vasisthasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to the sage Vasistha

steps.m: From Down Dog, roll onto the outer edge of the right foot into side plank on the right hand; lift the left leg and hold the big toe
Return to Down Dog
Repeat on the left hand
Return to Down Dog

alignment: Stack the shoulder over the wrist and press the floor away.
Keep the hips lifted in one line with the shoulders and feet.
Straighten the lifted leg before opening it wider.
modifications: Keep the top leg resting on the bottom leg (simple side plank).
Lower the bottom knee to the floor.
Hold the lifted leg with a strap.

visvamitrasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to the sage Visvamitra

steps.m: From Down Dog, step the right foot outside the right hand, hook the right leg over the right shoulder and straighten it; turn the back foot out, lift the left arm and hold the right foot
Return to Down Dog
Repeat on the left side
Return to Down Dog

alignment: Press the shoulder into the inner thigh to straighten the lifted leg.
Ground the outer edge of the back foot.
Rotate the chest up toward the top hand.
modifications: Keep the front knee bent and the top hand on the hip.
Use a block under the bottom hand.

kasyapasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to the sage Kasyapa
kasyapasana.note: The first of five postures with one foot behind the head; this one is practiced lying on the back.

steps.m: Jump through; place the right leg behind the head
Lie back with the left leg extended, hands in prayer at the chest
Come up
Jump through; place the left leg behind the head
Lie back, hands in prayer
Come up

alignment: Rotate the thigh outward from the hip before taking the leg back.
Draw the shoulder under the knee and lift the head back against the leg.
Keep the extended leg active and grounded.
modifications: Cradle the leg in the arms instead.
Practice Eka Pada Sirsasana from the Intermediate Series.

steps.m: Jump through; take the right leg behind the head, press the hands down and lift up with the left leg pointing straight up
Jump through; left leg behind the head, lift up with the right leg vertical

alignment: Keep the extended leg straight and reaching up.
Press firmly through the hands; lift the hips high.
Keep the leg secure behind the head before lifting.
modifications: Lift with the extended leg on the floor.
Practice Eka Pada Sirsasana C.

bhairavasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to Bhairava, a fierce form of Shiva

steps.m: Jump through; take the right leg behind the head
Place the right hand down and lift into a side plank, top arm reaching up
Lower and sit
Jump through; take the left leg behind the head
Side plank on the left hand
Lower and sit

alignment: Stack the shoulder over the wrist.
Lift the hips in line with the extended leg.
Keep the head pressing back into the leg.
modifications: Practice Vasisthasana in its simplest form.
Keep the bottom knee on the floor.

skandasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to Skanda, god of war

steps.m: Jump forward; standing on the left leg, take the right leg behind the head and fold forward, hands to the floor
Jump forward; standing on the right leg, take the left leg behind the head and fold forward

alignment: Fold from the hips with the standing leg straight.
Use the hands on the floor for balance before taking the leg back.
Keep the neck long against the leg.
modifications: Keep the standing knee bent.
Practice seated Eka Pada Sirsasana instead.

durvasasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to the sage Durvasa

steps.m: Jump through; take the right leg behind the head
Press up to stand on the left leg, hands in prayer
Lower down to sit
Jump through; take the left leg behind the head
Stand on the right leg, hands in prayer
Lower down to sit

alignment: Find the balance with the standing leg strong and straight.
Press the head back into the leg to lift the chest.
Steady gaze and slow breath help the balance.
modifications: Stand near a wall.
Practice Skandasana with the hands on the floor.

urdhva-kukkutasana.note: Practiced as three variations (A, B and C) that differ in how the lotus rests on the arms. Learn the details from your teacher.

steps.m: From Down Dog, come into Sirsasana and fold the legs into Padmasana
Lower the lotus onto the backs of the upper arms
Lift the head and balance on the hands

alignment: Round the back to lower the lotus with control.
Squeeze the knees toward the armpits.
Shift forward to balance as the head lifts.
modifications: Practice Kukkutasana from the Primary Series.
Practice Bakasana.

galavasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to the sage Galava

steps.m: From Down Dog, come into Sirsasana; take the right foot into half lotus
Lower the shin across the backs of the upper arms and extend the other leg behind; lift the head
Return to Sirsasana and change legs
Lower into the balance on the other side

alignment: Flex the foot of the lotus leg to protect the knee.
Keep the elbows over the wrists.
Reach back through the extended leg.
modifications: Keep the back foot on the floor.
Practice a figure-four squat with the hands on the floor.

eka-pada-bakasana.note: One knee rests on the upper arm while the other leg extends. A and B differ in the leg position.

steps.m: From Down Dog, come into Sirsasana
Lower one knee onto the upper arm, extend the other leg and lift the head
Return to Sirsasana and change legs
Lower into the balance on the other side

alignment: Place the knee high on the arm.
Keep the extended leg straight and strong.
Lean forward enough to lift the head.
modifications: Practice Bakasana.
Keep the extended leg's toes on the floor.

koundinyasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to the sage Koundinya
koundinyasana.note: A: both legs to one side with the top leg reaching sideways (twisted). B: one leg forward over the arm, the other extended back.

steps.m: From Down Dog, come into Sirsasana
Twist and lower the legs into the arm balance; lift the head
Return to Sirsasana
Lower into the balance on the other side

alignment: Bend the elbows like Chaturanga to make a shelf for the legs.
Keep the legs straight and active.
Look forward to counterbalance.
modifications: Keep one foot on the floor.
Practice side crow (Parsva Bakasana).

astavakrasana.meaning: Posture dedicated to the sage Astavakra
astavakrasana.note: A and B are the two sides.

steps.m: Jump through; hook the right leg over the right upper arm, cross the ankles and lift
Bend the elbows, lean forward and extend the legs out to the side
Come up and lower down
Jump through; hook the left leg over the left arm, cross the ankles and lift
Lean forward and extend the legs to the other side
Come up and lower down

alignment: Squeeze the thighs around the arm.
Keep the elbows hugging in as you lean.
Extend actively through both feet.
modifications: Stay lifted with bent knees.
Keep the feet on the floor and hold the leg on the arm.

steps.m: Jump through; take the left foot into half lotus, step the right foot over the left knee; twist right and bind
Jump through and repeat on the other side, twisting left

alignment: Set up the half lotus carefully, keeping the knee pain-free.
Lengthen up, then twist from the belly.
Keep both sit bones as grounded as possible.
modifications: Practice Ardha Matsyendrasana.
Keep the bottom leg folded without lotus.

viranchyasana.note: Seated postures that combine a foot-behind-the-head position with half lotus (A) or a bent knee (B). Learn the details from your teacher.

steps.m: Jump through; set up the right side: one foot behind the head, the other leg folded; hands in prayer
Jump through; set up the left side

alignment: Rotate the thigh outward from the hip before taking the foot back.
Keep the chest lifted and the head pressing back.
Never pull on the knee.
modifications: Practice Eka Pada Sirsasana A.
Cradle the leg in the arms.

steps.m: From Down Dog, come into Sirsasana with the fingers interlaced
Arch over and lower the feet to the floor; straighten the legs
Kick back up to Sirsasana

alignment: Press the forearms down and lift the shoulders.
Walk the feet out to straighten the legs, keeping the feet parallel.
Spread the backbend through the upper back.
modifications: Keep the knees bent.
Practice Urdhva Dhanurasana or a supported backbend over a bench.

steps.m: From Down Dog, come into Sirsasana
Arch over into Viparita Dandasana and lift the right leg to vertical
Lower the leg; lift the left leg
Kick back up to Sirsasana

alignment: Keep the hips lifted as the leg rises.
Lift the leg straight up from the hip without twisting.
modifications: Keep both feet down.
Lift the leg with the knee bent.

steps.m: Lower onto the chin and chest with the hands under the body; swing the legs up and over, bringing the feet toward the head

alignment: Keep the chin and chest grounded and the neck long.
Lift with strong arms pressing into the floor.
Come up gradually over many practices.
modifications: Practice Shalabhasana with the hands under the hips.
Lift only partway.

steps.m: Lower onto the chin and chest; swing the legs over and bring the feet down beside the head
Extend the arms out to the sides or hold the feet

alignment: Keep the chin and chest grounded.
Lower the feet slowly with control.
Keep breathing into the front of the body.
modifications: Practice Viparita Salabhasana.
Practice with a teacher's assistance.

hanumanasana.note: Often practiced upright with the arms overhead, then folding forward over the front leg.

steps.m: From Down Dog, step the right foot forward and slide into the splits; arms up, palms together
Fold forward over the front leg
Step the left foot forward and slide into the splits; arms up
Fold forward over the front leg

alignment: Square the hips forward; draw the back hip forward.
Keep the front kneecap facing up and the back knee facing down.
Lower gradually; keep the hands down for support until the hips reach the floor.
modifications: Place blocks under the hands and a bolster under the front hip.
Practice a half splits (Ardha Hanumanasana).

supta-trivikramasana.meaning: Reclining posture of Trivikrama (Vishnu's three strides)

steps.m: Jump through; exhale and lie down
Lift the right leg and draw it down beside the head, holding the heel with both hands
Release the leg
Lift the left leg and draw it down beside the head
Release the leg

alignment: Keep the bottom leg straight and pressing into the floor.
Keep the hips level as the leg comes down.
Draw the leg in line with the shoulder, not across the body.
modifications: Bend the bottom knee.
Use a strap around the lifted foot.

dighasana.note: A: the torso and lifted leg come parallel to the floor, arms reaching forward. B: rise onto the ball of the standing foot.

steps.m: From Samasthitih, raise the arms overhead
Hinge forward on the left leg, lifting the right leg until the body is parallel to the floor (A)
Rise onto the ball of the standing foot (B)
Lower the heel and return to standing
Raise the arms overhead
Hinge forward on the right leg (A)
Rise onto the ball of the foot (B)
Return to Samasthitih

alignment: Keep the hips level; don't let the lifted hip open.
Reach equally through the hands and the back heel.
Engage the standing leg strongly.
modifications: Rest the hands on blocks or a wall.
Keep the standing knee softly bent.

steps.m: From Samasthitih, lift the right leg, holding the heel, and draw it up beside the head
Lower the leg
Lift the left leg and draw it up beside the head
Lower the leg to Samasthitih

alignment: Keep the standing leg straight and the hips square.
Lift the leg in line with the shoulder.
Stand tall; don't lean away from the leg.
modifications: Use a strap around the foot.
Practice Utthita Hasta Padangusthasana.

natarajasana.meaning: Posture of Nataraja, lord of the dance

steps.m: From Samasthitih, bend the right knee and catch the foot overhead with both hands, elbows pointing up
Release the foot
Catch the left foot overhead with both hands
Release to Samasthitih

alignment: Kick the foot up and back into the hands.
Keep the hips square and the standing leg strong.
Lift the chest and keep the breath smooth.
modifications: Hold the foot with one hand and reach the other arm forward.
Use a strap around the foot.

steps.m: Lower onto the belly and press up with bent knees; reach back, hold the feet and draw them toward the head

alignment: Lengthen the front body before deepening the backbend.
Keep the knees hip-width.
Spread the bend evenly along the spine.
modifications: Practice Kapotasana or Bhekasana.
Use a strap around the feet.

steps.m: From Down Dog, bring the right shin forward and extend the left leg back; bend the back knee and catch the foot overhead with both hands
Bring the left shin forward and catch the right foot overhead

alignment: Square the hips forward; keep the front foot flexed.
Lift the chest before reaching back.
Elbows point up as you hold the foot.
modifications: Use a strap around the back foot.
Keep the hands on the floor in a simple pigeon.
